whyChoose.title: Why Reach Out Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Clock
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within 2 years of the incident, and claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as 6 months. Waiting too long can close the door on your options entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering Claims
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life, unlike many other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That means getting advice doesn't add to your financial stress.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Willits?
items.answer: In California, you generally have 2 years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government agency or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as 6 months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly at fault doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of responsibility.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Willits?
items.answer: Public collision records point to higher volumes along Highway 101, Highway 20, S Main Street, and Main Street, with reports also tending to peak on Thursday afternoons between 1 and 3 p.m. These are neutral counts of reported activity, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is completely free, and attorneys in the network work on contingency — meaning they only get paid if they win or settle your case.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. We simply help connect injured people in Willits with an independent attorney who can evaluate their situation.
